title: Infra Playbook: GPU Fleet, CI/CD, and Terraform/IaC Modules
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates operational standards, Terraform/IaC module patterns, CI/CD pipeline templates, and runbook procedures for managing Redwood's GPU fleet and related infra (cloud accounts, networking, CI/CD). It is intended as the canonical team wiki reference for infra engineers and SREs onboarding to GPU-related workstreams.

Goals:
- Maintain predictable capacity for model serving with clear scaling thresholds and ownership.
- Provide reusable Terraform/IaC modules for GPU instances, networking, and account-level controls.
- Standardize CI/CD for infra changes with safety gates and automated testing.
- Document runbooks for common capacity incidents and maintenance operations.

1) High-level architecture and ownership
- Control plane: infra-team-managed AWS account (org-root), VPCs per environment (prod/staging/dev).
- GPU fleet: Dedicated GPU node groups (k8s node pools) and Dedicated baremetal pools for high-throughput inference.
- Owners:
  - GPU fleet capacity and autoscaling: eng-sre
  - Terraform/IaC modules and pipeline templates: infra-engineering
  - Cloud account and networking control: infra-security

2) Capacity planning and SLOs
- SLOs (applies to production inference clusters):
  - 99th-percentile tail latency degradation due to node scarcity: <= 2% monthly
  - Fleet availability (nodes Ready): 99.9% monthly
  - GPU utilization target window: 40%-70% (target average 55%)
- Thresholds and escalation:
  - Warning: average utilization > 70% for 24 hours -> capacity review + scale-up plan
  - Critical: average utilization > 85% for 6 hours -> take immediate corrective action (scale or shed noncritical workloads)
  - Underutilization: average utilization < 30% for 7 days -> investigate rightsizing/packing opportunities

3) Terraform/IaC module patterns (recommended structure)
- Module names and purpose:
  - modules/gpu-nodegroup: create node pools with GPU AMI, taints, kubelet config, instance types (p4d, a10, a100 variants).
  - modules/networking: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways, security groups for k8s and dedicated hosts.
  - modules/iam-baseline: scoped roles, instance profiles, KMS key attachment patterns.
  - modules/baremetal-pool: terraform-managed reserved instances/baremetal orchestration (where applicable).
  - modules/ci-pipeline: reusable GitHub Actions / CircleCI workflows for plan/apply gates.
- Example usage (HCL snippet):
  ```hcl
  module "gpu_pool_prod" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood.ai/infra/modules.git//gpu-nodegroup"
    name   = "prod-gpu-pool-1"
    instance_types = ["p4d.24xlarge", "p4d.12xlarge"]
    desired_capacity = 20
    min_size = 5
    max_size = 50
    taints = [{key = "dedicated", value = "inference", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE"}]
  }
  ```
- Module design guidelines:
  - Keep modules small and opinionated. One logical resource per module where possible.
  - Provide feature flags (booleans) to opt in/out of advanced configs (GPUDirect, ENA settings).
  - All modules must expose tags, owner, and cost-center fields.
  - Avoid embedding environment-specific values; prefer variables and workspaces.

4) Git/GitOps and CI/CD patterns
- Repo layout:
  - infra/
    - modules/
    - live/
      - prod/
      - staging/
      - dev/
- Branching and PR policy:
  - All changes require an approved PR with at least one reviewer from infra-engineering.
  - Small, incremental changes preferred. Breaking changes need an ADR and rollout plan.
- Pipeline template (GitHub Actions example):
  ```yaml
  name: Terraform CI
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    validate:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Setup Terraform
          uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
        - name: Terraform Init
          run: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}"
        - name: Terraform Validate
          run: terraform validate
        - name: Terraform Plan
          run: terraform plan -out=plan.out
        - name: Upload plan
          uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
          with:
            name: plan-out
            path: plan.out
  ```
- Apply policy and gating:
  - Only staging and dev applies allowed via automation. Prod applies require a manual approval step (GitHub environment protection or self-serve approvals in Octopus).
  - All prod applies must be run by oncall or an approved release engineer.

5) CI/CD best practices for GPU infra changes
- Must include automated cost estimation step for changes that modify instance types or counts.
- Run terraform plan against a dry-run cluster where possible (k8s resources validated by kubeval).
- Add automated tests to validate: IAM least-privilege, network reachability (internal e2e smoke), and node boot success (cloud-init logs).

6) Runbooks and common operational procedures
- Incident: Node shortage / scaling fails
  1. Triage: Check autoscaler logs (k8s cluster-autoscaler) and Terraform cloud run logs.
  2. Verify limits: Check AWS account EC2 quota for GPU instance family (Service Quotas console).
  3. Immediate mitigation:
     - If quota-limited, open a quota increase request to AWS Support and enable fallback pool with compatible non-preferred instance types.
     - Scale down batch/low-priority jobs: tag workloads with priority labels and use kube-scheduler preemption where configured.
  4. Longer-term: increase desired_capacity or add an on-demand baremetal pool.
  5. Post-incident: create a postmortem, update capacity thresholds if needed.

- Maintenance: rolling kernel/driver upgrades on GPU nodes
  - Step 1: Create a canary nodegroup (1-2 nodes) in a noncritical AZ using same AMI/kernel.
  - Step 2: Drain a canary and apply kernel/driver upgrade; smoke test inference containers for 60 minutes.
  - Step 3: If stable, roll to 10% of fleet, then 50%, then 100% with verification gates.
  - Rollback: If kernel/driver mismatch occurs, revert to previous AMI and mark nodes as unschedulable until fixed.

7) Networking and cloud account notes
- VPC design:
  - Separate VPCs per environment with peering or Transit Gateway for shared services.
  - Use private subnets for GPU nodes and NAT gateways for controlled egress.
- Security groups and endpoints:
  - Minimum required egress to S3, ECR, and AWS KMS.
  - Use VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB to avoid public subnet egress.

8) Alerts and dashboards (ownership: eng-platform)
- Essential alerts:
  - GPU node Ready status drops below 99% (pager)
  - Autoscaler failing to scale for >5m (pager)
  - Average GPU utilization >85% for 6h (pager)
  - Terraform apply failures in prod (investigate, page infra oncall)
- Dashboards to maintain:
  - Fleet utilization by instance family and AZ
  - Per-cluster autoscaler events and pending pods
  - Cost burn by instance type and team tags

9) Oncall and runbook ownership
- Primary oncall: eng-sre rotating schedule (escalate to infra-engineering after 15m if not resolved).
- Playbook ownership: infra-engineering must review this playbook quarterly.

10) Useful CLI snippets and commands
- Check GPU quotas (AWS CLI):
  ```bash
  aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-XXXXXX
  ```
- Check k8s node GPU readiness:
  ```bash
  kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -i gpu
  kubectl describe node <node-name> | egrep "GPU|taints|kubelet"
  ```
- Terraform plan with cost estimate (example using infracost):
  ```bash
  infracost break-down --path infra/live/prod --format json > infracost-prod.json
  terraform plan -out plan.out
  ```

11) Templates and links
- GitHub Actions pipeline templates: infra/.github/workflows/terraform-ci.yml
- Module registry: git@repo.redwood.ai:infra/modules.git (see README in modules root)
- Runbook: confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026

Appendix: Operational checklists
- Pre-scaling checklist:
  - Confirm quotas and reservations
  - Confirm AMI/kernel compatibility with new instance families
  - Ensure alerting and dashboards are enabled for the new pool
- Post-deploy checklist:
  - Confirm nodes report Ready within 6 minutes
  - Run smoke inference at 10 RPS per node for 5 minutes
  - Validate cost estimate matches forecast within 15%

If you are editing this page: add PR links and keep the module versioning table up to date. If you need an exception (e.g., one-off instance type changes), file a risk-and-exceptions entry in security-and-compliance.
